design_rationale:
WHY A GOOD TEST (revision 2). Desmond Adeyemi (Meadowlark Commit 5, 14.00 kW, MD BGE, dual billed, active) asks on 2026-11-12 to make good the 2026-10-01 card payment of his August charge that his card issuer reversed on 2026-11-09, and to pay what he owes today from his checking account. The replacement payment is fixed only after every returned payment carries its returned-payment fee and not until the charge of the month named on the latest returned-payment line, past grace and unpaid, carries its late fee; at the opening the reversal has no fee and the reopened August charge has no late fee. The agent reads both waits from the payment rule, books the two fees (5 and 6 factors) and then works out the replacement payment (4 factors). The ledger follows the payment-application order as the payment rules overwrite it: the July charge was paid late with its fee on 2026-09-20, the card payment settled August (the oldest open line on 2026-10-01), and the 30.00 of 2026-11-10 settled the reopened August charge because the disputed September charge is settled by no payment while its dispute is open.

SCOPE. Task 1 claims home_ext_reversed_payment_replacement (root, owner=user), home_ext_returned_payment_fee and home_ext_reopened_late_fee (state_due), tools pay_reversed_payment_replacement_378a2026, assess_returned_payment_fee_1f86a5ed, assess_reopened_charge_late_fee_2381e61d; disjoint from task 0. Draw [5,6,4]: returned-payment fee 5, reopened late fee 6, payment 4. The reopened-charge late fee mirrors the overdue-charge late fee's six ladders; the payment's dispute-hold, pending-statement and fee-share ladders mirror the final-balance payment's.

PROBLEM TREE. Edge -> returned-payment fee (value_input, gate pay_fees, state, affirmative): "The replacement payment is fixed only after every returned payment on the subscription carries its returned-payment fee, wherever the returned-payment fee rule writes one." False at opening: the 2026-11-09 returned line names the 2026-10-01 payment and no fee refers to it (the 2026-05-08 return carries its fee). Edge -> reopened late fee (value_input, gate rvs_fees, state, negated): "The replacement payment is not fixed until the charge of the statement month named on the latest returned-payment line, once its late-fee grace period has passed with the charge unpaid, carries a late fee line referring to it, wherever the reopened-charge late fee rule writes one." False at opening: August charge due 2026-10-10, reopened, past grace, unpaid, undisputed, no fee. The writes commute (recomputed both orders); deletion runs are in prerequisite_closure.edge_load_bearing.

FACTORS. Returned-payment fee: item base (method; returned amount 200 or more -> greater of the plan fee and 10 percent), item kind (parameter; card reversal), committed term (parameter, R1 plan term; replaces the round-1 reversal-time factor, struck as an invented mechanism), repeat (parameter; ach return of 2026-05-08 and card reversal of 2026-11-09), household income (parameter, cross-difficulty waitlist, multi-source; reservation of 1.00 kW queued 2026-03-10 within the account's headroom). The fee is limited to the fee ceiling and, for a returned check, to the plan fee. Reopened late fee: priced amount (method; return recorded for August -> full charge), months (1 whole month), household income (waitlist), repeat (July fee of 2026-09-17), size (150 or more), banked share. Replacement payment: dispute hold (method; September charge), pending statement (method; the October credit posted 2026-11-09 is not yet priced and October has no estimate -> its coming charge is added), household-income fee share (parameter, cross waitlist), reversal kind (parameter; card). Every figure is in the computations' factor_trace / factor_sensitivity.

SEED. 41 postings 2023-06..2026-10 (October posted 2026-11-09, invoiced 2026-11-14), charges at credit x 0.88, ACH payments on time through June 2026 except March (ach of 2026-05-04 returned 2026-05-08, fee priced by the returned-payment fee rule that day, charge repaid 2026-05-11, fee paid 2026-05-26); July charge paid late 2026-09-20 with its fee of 2026-09-17 (overdue-charge rule that day); August paid by card 2026-10-01, reversed 2026-11-09; 30.00 ach 2026-11-10 for August; September charge open (due 2026-11-05, grace to 2026-11-15) and disputed 2026-11-08 (decision due 2026-12-08); true-ups of years 1-3 above the 85 percent guarantee with no resize; waitlist reservation queued since 2026-03-10. Nothing else is owed at the opening (no removal notice is possible, no fee on the September charge yet, October not yet invoiced).

PERSONA. Practical mechanic; volunteers the reversal and the wish to pay today from checking; identity on request; the 30.00 payment, the November 8th dispute and the waitlist only on request; passive agreement; pays the stated amount himself by ach.

SOLUTION. Reads: customers, identity, subscriptions, utility accounts, projects, billing, credits, allocations, requests, reviews, waitlist, access. Writes: assess_returned_payment_fee_1f86a5ed (the 2026-10-01 payment, 2026-08, due 2026-12-03), assess_reopened_charge_late_fee_2381e61d (August charge, 2026-08, due 2026-12-03), then pay_reversed_payment_replacement_378a2026 by the caller (recorded against 2026-08, ach). Verification: /tmp/residential_bill_credits_and_charges_0082/gen1*.py and task1*.py.
user_scenario: You are Desmond Adeyemi, 45, a transit bus mechanic in Baltimore, Maryland, with a Meadowlark residential solar share on your house. On October 1st you paid your Meadowlark solar bill online with your credit card, but in early November your card company reversed that payment by mistake while sorting out a fraud claim on a different purchase. You are calling to make that reversed payment good today so your solar account is back in order. You open by explaining, in a slightly rushed and practical way, that your card company reversed the solar payment you made on October 1st and you want to fix it and pay what you owe on the solar subscription today. This time you want to pay from your checking account, and you will type the bank details into Meadowlark's secure payment page yourself; you never read card or bank numbers to anyone and you have nothing stored with Meadowlark. When the agent asks you to confirm who you are, you give your phone number, 6515550113, and if they need a second detail your billing ZIP code, 21216; if they ask for your email it is d.adeyemi.home@gmail.com. You do not know any account or reference numbers. Only if the agent asks whether you have paid anything since the reversal do you say you put 30 dollars through online on November 10th. Only if the agent asks about the September charge or any dispute do you say that on November 8th you filed a dispute about the September charge because it looked high to you, and you are waiting to hear back. Only if the agent asks whether you hold anything else with Meadowlark do you say you are on their income-eligible waiting list for a second share; nothing else. If the agent explains that something has to be added to the account or worked out before the amount can be given, you tell them to go ahead. When the agent gives you the amount to pay today and hands you the secure payment step, you complete it yourself for exactly that amount, choosing ach as the method; you do not argue about the figure or ask for anything to be removed. Once the payment goes through, you thank the agent and say that is all you needed.
